(b) Give the chemical name of rust. [2]
(c) Describe two methods of preventing rusting and explain how each works. [4]
(d) Why is aluminium slower to corrode in air than iron? [2]
questions.answer: (a) oxygen and water; (b) hydrated iron(III) oxide; (c) paint/oil/galvanising/sacrificial; (d) oxide layer

steps.d: Paint/oil: barrier to air and water. Galvanising / zinc: barrier and sacrificial protection.
Aluminium forms a thin, unreactive oxide layer that protects the metal.

questions.answer: (a) energy not created or destroyed; (b) 200 J; (c) chemical → electrical → light/heat; (d) free electrons / vibrating particles

steps.d: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transferred from one store to another.
Free electrons and vibrating particles pass energy through the metal.

questions.markscheme: 10 mark(s). Answer: (a) energy not created or destroyed; (b) 200 J; (c) chemical → electrical → light/heat; (d) free electrons / vibrating particles

questions.text:

(b) State Ohm’s law. [2]
(c) A resistor of 4 Ω is connected to a 6 V supply. Calculate the current. [3]
(d) State one difference between a series and a parallel circuit. [2]
questions.answer: (b) V = IR; (c) 1.5 A; (d) series: same current; parallel: same voltage across branches

steps.d: Cell: long and short line. Resistor: rectangle. Ammeter: circle with A, in series.
V = IR (current proportional to p.d. at constant temperature).
Series: one path, same current. Parallel: branches, same p.d. across each branch.

questions.markscheme: 10 mark(s). Answer: (b) V = IR; (c) 1.5 A; (d) series: same current; parallel: same voltage across branches

questions.text:
(a) State one adaptation of a palisade mesophyll cell and link it to photosynthesis. [2]
(b) State one adaptation of a red blood cell for oxygen transport. [2]
(c) Describe how a sperm cell is adapted to reach and fertilise an egg. [3]
(d) Explain why ciliated cells line the trachea. [3]
questions.answer: (a) many chloroplasts / packed cells; (b) haemoglobin / biconcave / no nucleus; (c) flagellum, mitochondria, acrosome; (d) sweep mucus

steps.d: Many chloroplasts / close to upper surface — absorb light.
Haemoglobin; biconcave disc; no nucleus — more space for haemoglobin.
Flagellum for swimming; mitochondria for energy; acrosome enzymes to penetrate the egg.

Growth and repair of tissues / enzymes / some hormones.
Fibre cannot be digested; adds bulk and helps peristalsis / prevents constipation.

steps.d: Solid: close, regular, vibrate. Gas: far apart, random rapid motion.
Gas particles have large spaces so can be pushed closer. Liquid particles are already close.

questions.answer: (a) i = r; (b) slows, towards the normal; (c) sound needs a medium; light is EM; (d) pitch–frequency, loudness–amplitude
